title: Notosan — scroll-driven nature parallax hero
notes: Travel site hero for a fictional Japanese nature park brand, "Notosan." Originally analyzed as a 10s auto-advancing carousel, but that recreation felt static/choppy in practice. This prompt is the corrected version: a real scroll-driven parallax build (three normal-flow 100vh sections + fixed crossfaded background layers + IntersectionObserver reveals), validated end-to-end and confirmed fluid.
recreation_prompt:
Build a scroll-driven, multi-section hero for a fictional Japanese nature-park travel brand called "Notosan." The page has THREE full-height sections the user scrolls through normally (this is not a fixed/absolute-stacked single-screen carousel) — each section swaps in its own full-viewport background photo and reveals its own heading/copy as it scrolls into view.

GLOBAL LAYOUT:
- `html { scroll-behavior: smooth; }`. Body is black, white text, `overflow-x: hidden`.
- Fixed navbar pinned to the top of the whole page (not per-section): wordmark "Notosan" on the left; nav links "Community / About / Support / Contact" plus a pill-shaped "Register" button (1px white border, fills white with black text on hover) on the right. Background is a gradient from `rgba(0,0,0,0.7)` at the top fading to transparent, so it reads over any photo beneath it. `padding: 2rem 4rem`, `z-index: 100`.
- Typography: pair a serif display face (e.g. Playfair Display) for headings with a geometric sans (e.g. Inter) for everything else — this contrast is part of the look, don't use one font for both.

BACKGROUND LAYERS (the parallax mechanism):
- Three `position: fixed; top:0; left:0; width:100%; height:120vh; z-index:-1;` divs, one per section, each with its own `background-image` (real photography — a vibrant mountain at sunrise/dusk for section 1, a mystical blue waterfall for section 2, a glowing lush forest for section 3), `background-size: cover`, plus a `::after` dark overlay (`rgba(0,0,0,0.4)`) so white text stays legible over any photo.
- All three start at `opacity: 0` with `transition: opacity 1s ease-in-out`; only the currently-relevant one carries `.active` (`opacity: 1`) at a time — crossfade, never a hard cut or a slide.
- On scroll, apply a continuous subtle parallax drift to every background layer (not just the active one, so whichever fades in next is already correctly positioned): `scrollFraction = scrollY / (document.body.scrollHeight - windowHeight)`, `translateY = -(scrollFraction * windowHeight * 0.2)`, applied as `transform: translateY(...)`. The 120vh height (20vh taller than the viewport) is exactly what gives this drift room to move without exposing an edge.
- Track which section currently owns the background by comparing `scrollY` against each section's `offsetTop - windowHeight/2`, checked from the last section backward (so the furthest-down threshold crossed wins); only touch the DOM (`classList.add/remove('active')`) when the winning section actually changes, not on every scroll tick.

FOREGROUND SECTIONS:
- Each `<section>` is a normal, real 100vh block (`display:flex; flex-direction:column; justify-content:center; padding: 0 10%;`) — three of them stacked in normal document flow, so the page is genuinely 300vh tall and scrolls like a regular page, not a pinned/absolute single screen.
- Section 1 (hero): no alignment override, so content sits left via the default flex stretch inside its `max-width: 600px` wrapper. Kicker-style subtitle ("Journey to new frontiers, Journey to Noto Nature Park", small, letter-spaced 3px, muted white), a massive serif headline ("VISITE", ~7rem, letter-spacing 5px, line-height 1), 2-3 lines of body copy, and a primary CTA: a transparent button with uppercase tracked text plus a circular outlined play-icon badge (50x50px) that fills white with a black icon on hover, and the whole button shifts `translateX(10px)` on hover.
- Section 2: same structure but `align-items: flex-end; text-align: right;` (content sits on the right). Small numbered tag ("02 / Experience"), serif section title ("Tranquility", ~5rem), body copy, and a secondary CTA: a plain text link ("Learn more →") whose gap between text and arrow grows from 0.8rem to 1.2rem on hover (the arrow visibly slides away, not translateX).
- Section 3: mirrors section 2 but `align-items: flex-start; text-align: left;` (back on the left). Tag ("03 / Habitat"), title ("Biodiversity"), copy, same secondary-link CTA style.

SCROLL REVEALS (IntersectionObserver, not scroll-position math):
- Each section's content wrapper starts as `opacity:0; transform: translateY(50px);` with `transition: all 0.8s cubic-bezier(0.25,0.46,0.45,0.94);`.
- An `IntersectionObserver` with `{ threshold: 0.3 }` toggles a `.active` class on whichever wrapper is intersecting — add it back off every time the element leaves the viewport too, so the reveal replays if the user scrolls back up and down again, rather than firing once and staying done.
- Once `.active`, the wrapper's direct children (kicker/heading/copy/CTA) each independently run a `fadeInUp` keyframe (`opacity 0→1`, `translateY(30px)→0`, 0.8s) with staggered `animation-delay` of 0.1s/0.3s/0.5s/0.7s in DOM order, so the text cascades in piece by piece instead of arriving as one block.

RESPONSIVE: below ~768px, hide the nav links (keep logo + Register), and drop the hero title/section titles to roughly 4rem/3rem with reduced section padding.

title: Kamui — dark-fantasy blockchain card game landing page
notes: Real coded project (Next.js 16 + Framer Motion + Tailwind v4) at C:\Documents\Self Projects\kamui-game — read every component's source rather than guessing from pixels. One catch: the checked-in HeroSection.tsx still has a literal `{/* Background Placeholder */}` Unsplash photo; the video the user supplied shows the actual intended illustrated hero art (pagoda on a hill, mountains, bridge, cranes, lanterns, cherry blossoms), so the prompt below describes that real target art, not the placeholder still sitting in the code. Everything else (animation mechanics, other 3 sections) matches the source exactly.
recreation_prompt:
Build a full multi-section landing page for a dark-fantasy Japanese blockchain card game called "KAMUI." Stack: Next.js + Framer Motion for every animation described below, Tailwind for layout/utility classes.

PALETTE (exact tokens): background #060314 (deep midnight indigo), panel #150e2d (dark purple, also used for button text), accent magenta #e024a5, accent pink #fbcce7, accent gold #f59e0b, off-white foreground #f3f4f6.

TYPOGRAPHY: pair a serif/gothic display face (e.g. Cinzel) for wordmarks/headings with a clean grotesque sans (e.g. Inter) for everything else.

NAVBAR (fixed across the whole page): `position:fixed; top:0; z-index:50`, slides down on load (`initial y:-100 → animate y:0`, 0.5s easeOut). Transparent with `py-6` at the top; past `scrollY > 50` it switches to `bg-[#060314]/80 backdrop-blur-md` with a bottom border, drop shadow, and reduced `py-4` (all via `transition-all duration-300`). "KAMUI" wordmark left (gains a white text-glow on hover); right side has uppercase tracked links ("Game / Cards / Community / Esports") each with a 2px underline that grows `width:0→100%` on hover in glowing magenta, plus a Twitch link whose icon gets a purple (`#9146FF`) drop-shadow glow on hover.

SECTION 1 — HERO (`min-h-screen`, content pinned right via `flex items-center justify-end`, generous padding, `overflow-hidden`):
- Background: a full-bleed flat-illustration scene — a wooden pagoda/shrine on a grassy hill, layered mountains behind in a pink-to-lavender dusk gradient, a curved wooden bridge crossing water in the foreground, two cranes standing in the shallows, warm glowing paper lanterns, soft god-ray light — NOT a photo. Overlay a `linear-gradient(to right, rgba(6,3,20,0.8), rgba(6,3,20,0.3))` (darker where there's no text, lighter behind the content) plus a full-bleed magenta div at 10% opacity with `mix-blend-mode:overlay` for color-grade.
- A giant watermark: the kanji "神威" at `text-[40rem] font-black`, absolute, vertically centered, hanging off the right edge (`right:-5%`), 3% opacity, non-interactive — pure texture.
- Cherry-blossom petals: 30 client-generated divs, each randomized `delay` (0–10s), `duration` (10–20s), `startX`. Petal shape: small (`w-3 h-4`), pink at 60% opacity, asymmetric `border-radius:50% 0 50% 50%`, 1px blur. Animate `initial={{y:-50, x:startX, opacity:0, rotate:0}}` → `animate={{y:'110vh', x:startX-100, opacity:[0,1,1,0], rotate:360}}`, linear ease, `repeat:Infinity` — falling, drifting left, fading in then out, spinning once, forever.
- Content (right-aligned, `max-width:42rem`), staggering in on mount: (1) "KAMUI" wordmark, `text-7xl`/`text-9xl`, bold, `tracking-[0.2em]`, white with a soft white text-glow, slides in from `opacity:0,x:50→opacity:1,x:0` over 0.8s at `delay:0.2`; (2) "A Blockchain Card Game" subtitle, same slide-in, `delay:0.4`; (3) "Join The Waitlist" pill button — white bg, panel-color text, bold uppercase, glows white, hover turns accent-pink and scales to 1.05 — enters `opacity:0,y:20→opacity:1,y:0`, `delay:0.6`; (4) "Plays on macOS, Windows & Linux" caption, plain fade-in, `delay:0.8`.

SECTION 2 — GAME INTRO (`min-h-screen`, `bg-[#060314]`, a soft gold radial glow at 70%/50%): two-column grid, both columns doing `whileInView` fade+slide reveals (`viewport:{once:true, margin:'-100px'}`, 0.8s). Left: magenta kicker "Powered by Ethereum", big serif heading "A STRATEGIC CARD GAME", body copy about Feudal-Japan-meets-dark-fantasy strategic combat, then a row of small pill badges (icon + label) for "macOS / Windows / Linux", "iPhone / Android", "iPad Pro" on a dark panel background. Right: a tall (600px) rounded image panel with a gold glow border showing a moody in-game/interior illustration, gradient candlelight overlay, slides in from the right 0.2s after the left column.

SECTION 3 — 3D CARD CAROUSEL (`min-h-screen`, `bg-[#150e2d]` panel color, a 5%-opacity seigaiha (scale-wave) SVG pattern tiled behind everything): a magenta "0X / 03" position indicator above a `perspective:1000px` stage holding 3 cards. Cards are positioned by their index offset from the current one: `x = relativeIndex * 250px`, `z = 50 if center else -100`, `scale = 1 if center else 0.8`, `opacity = 1 center / 0.5 adjacent / 0 further`, animated with Framer Motion (`duration:0.6, ease:[0.23,1,0.32,1]`). Each card is double-sided (`transformStyle:preserve-3d`, `backfaceVisibility:hidden` on both faces): front face shows a diamond emblem in a circle and the "KAMUI" wordmark with a pulsing "CLICK TO FLIP" hint (only on the centered, unflipped card); clicking the centered card flips it (`rotateY 0→180`, spring `stiffness:60, damping:15`) to reveal a back face with an image, a glowing title, and description text. Clicking a side card instead re-centers the carousel on it. Below: text "← Previous" / "Next →" buttons flanking a thin progress bar that fills (`width` tween, 0.5s easeOut) to `(index+1)/total`, glowing magenta.

SECTION 4 — YOKAI SECTION (`min-h-screen`, near-black `#050212`, a firefly particle field): same text-left/image-right grid as section 2, but the image panel reads differently — a smaller framed square-ish card (not a wide rectangle) with visible decorative corner brackets, giving it a museum-placard feel next to section 2's plain wide photo panel. 25 fireflies (gold, glowing, 2px, blurred) spawn from below the fold and float upward with random horizontal drift and fade in/out, looping on random durations (5–13s) — same generation pattern as the hero's petals but drifting up instead of falling down. Left column: gold kicker "Own Your Cards", heading "SUMMON YOKAI CREATURES", copy about collecting 200+ ERC-721 Yokai NFTs, and an outlined (not filled) pill CTA "Join The Waitlist" that tints on hover and scales down slightly on tap (`whileHover`/`whileTap`). Right column: a framed square-ish illustration panel (a fox-masked yokai character) with a magenta glow border, backdrop blur, and four small decorative L-shaped corner brackets top/bottom-left/right — enters with a spring scale (`0.9→1`, `stiffness:50`).
